spots.s: Mile-and-a-half of wine bars, boat docks, and skyline right on the water — the easiest great first date downtown.
The city's best 90 minutes: skyscraper stories from the water aboard Chicago's First Lady — a can't-miss date.
The Bean, free Pritzker Pavilion concerts, and Maggie Daley's gardens over the bridge — downtown's living room.
World-top-ten museum; the Impressionist wing and Thorne Miniature Rooms make an unhurried rainy-day date.
Free entry under the world's largest Tiffany glass dome — swing through before a Loop dinner.

spots.n: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
spots.s: The U-505 submarine and coal mine still thrill as an adult — give Hyde Park's giant a full afternoon.
Skyline-backed sand with volleyball courts everywhere — summer's easiest low-pressure hang.
The Hancock's 94th-floor view with a bar and the TILT ledge — beats the Skydeck lines at sunset.
Acres of jungle under glass, free — a warm, secret-feeling date in the dead of winter.
Bleachers, sun, and an Old Style at the 1914 cathedral of day baseball — take the Red Line, not the car.
The institution that minted SNL casts — a guaranteed-laughs date in Old Town.
Locals' favorite skyline view from Hyde Park's limestone steps — bring a picnic, stay for sunset.
Skip the mall, come for the free fireworks over the lake — Wednesdays 9p and Saturdays 10p all summer.
Free, open 365 days, and gorgeous at dusk — pair it with the lily pool and conservatory next door.
Free Pilsen gem — pair it with a mural walk down 18th Street and a taqueria stop.

spots.n: Wicker Park crawl (Reckless Records + Myopic Books)
spots.s: Record bins, used books, and coffee along Milwaukee Ave — the classic browse-and-talk afternoon date.
The postcard skyline panorama from the peninsula — walk it at blue hour even if you skip the sky shows.
Quiet Japanese garden on Jackson Park's wooded island — feels a thousand miles from the Loop.
1929 movie palace with organ preludes and 70mm runs — the film-buff date spot on Southport.
Paddle the river canyon between skyscrapers — beginner-friendly guided sunset trips from the Riverwalk.
385 acres of gardens a half hour north — free entry, and the bonsai collection is world-class.

nightlife.s: House music's home club since 1982 in Frankie Knuckles' city — Queen! on Sundays with Derrick Carter is a rite of passage.
Subterranean River North den where serious house and techno heads dance until 4a (5a Saturdays).
Nine bars and a big room of touring house/EDM names — River North's proper megaclub since 2004.
Lincoln Park's slick big-room club — hip-hop and open-format nights with serious lights and production.
Uptown boutique club on a 25,000-watt system — house, Afrobeats, amapiano, and hip-hop with zero dress code.
The old Berlin space reborn in 2026 as a 4am dance club on Belmont — the new late-late floor.
Red-lit Logan Square dance dive — free entry, nightly DJs heavy on hip-hop, and a skee-ball corner.
Logan Square's all-vinyl Latin/tropical bar — cumbia and salsa spill onto the floor till 2a.
Free-entry Logan Square listening room — jazz early, DJs late, award-winning cocktails.
The room that started Chicago's cocktail renaissance — candlelit, no-phones booths built for conversation.
Capone-era jazz shrine in Uptown, cash only — Sunday's Uptown Poetry Slam invented the format.
Two stages of blues seven nights till 4a — Lincoln Park institution since 1968, kitchen open late.
Family-run West Side blues lounge — the real thing, far off the tourist circuit since 1984.
1937 art-deco time capsule on Humboldt Park — killer sound system and live swing, soul, and country nights.
A shack behind a factory with the best-booked small stage in town — everyone talks to everyone.

eats.s: Chef Otto Phan's brash, top-tier Edomae counter in Logan Square — Chicago's most-argued-about splurge.
Phan's lower-priced sibling counter two doors down — the smart first rung on the omakase ladder.
Chef Sangtae Park's serene 10-seat West Loop counter — precise Edomae with zero theatrics.
B.K. Park's Michelin-starred West Loop omakase — polished, warm, and very date-appropriate.
Hip-hop on the speakers and hand rolls on the counter — the loud, fun entry point in River North.
Lincoln Park's reliable neighborhood omakase — chef's-choice quality without downtown ceremony.
Reddit's 'Ramen Lord' gone brick-and-mortar — nationally lauded miso bowls; book five weeks out or line up early.
Sixteen stools in a West Loop basement for fiery tonkotsu — pass the wait with a highball upstairs.
Boka's three-story Japanese showpiece — sushi upstairs, izakaya den in the basement.
Julia Momose's West Loop dining bar — cocktail omakase that doubles as the city's classiest date seat.
Old-school charcoal KBBQ on Western with a 30-dish banchan spread — go hungry, stay late.
Gruff, beloved 1980s-vintage Korean grill in Lincoln Square — bulgogi smoke, soju, no frills.
Beard-winning duo's vinyl listening bar in Avondale — tteokbokki, highballs, and nightly DJ sets.
Michelin-starred Filipino in Ukrainian Village — pastry counter by day, tasting menu by night.
Pilsen's Beard-nominated Vietnamese — clay-pot fish, crispy wings, and a great cocktail patio.

chinese.s: Chinatown's dim sum flagship — har gow, BBQ pork bao, and sticky rice in a big, easy room on Archer.

chinese.n: Qing Xiang Yuan Dumplings 庆祥园
chinese.s: Award-winning jiaozi house — lamb-coriander and crab-roe soup dumplings worth the trip alone.
Tony Hu's 1998 flagship — dry chili chicken 辣子鸡 and mapo tofu that anchor Chicago Sichuan cooking.
Chengdu-style refinement in Lincoln Park — boiled fish 水煮鱼 and tea-smoked ribs, the closest thing to 四川 home cooking.
Watch the noodle-puller work the dough — la mian and soup dumplings on Archer since 2007.
Chengdu's famous hot pot chain in a carved-wood, red-lantern room — order the butter-chili broth 牛油锅.
Chinatown's oldest bakery (1986) — dan tat egg tarts and BBQ pork buns for the Wentworth stroll.
Chicago's biggest Chinese market — two floors of groceries plus Qiao Lin Hotpot and a serious food court.
Blade-Runner-lit cocktail bar hidden behind Moon Palace — 50 Best-listed drinks with a DJ in the corner.

chinese.n: Ping Tom Memorial Park 谭继平纪念公园
chinese.s: Chinatown's riverside stunner — pagoda pavilion, skyline views, and a water taxi straight to the Loop.
James Beard 'America's Classic' on the Argyle strip — order the whole Beijing duck feast ahead.
Two-level plaza of bubble tea, bakeries, and zodiac bronzes — the after-dinner wander.
Chinatown's full-service grocery for Sichuan pantry runs — 豆瓣酱, fresh noodles, live fish.
Massive Asian grocery and food hall steps from the Loop — stock the pantry without a suburban drive.

chinese.n: Chinese American Museum of Chicago 美洲华裔博物馆
chinese.s: Small, moving museum of Chicago's Chinese story on 23rd Street — pair with a Cermak food crawl.

chinese.n: Chinatown Lunar New Year Parade 农历新年游行
chinese.s: Lions, dragons, and floats down Wentworth the Sunday after 春节 — stake out Cermak & Wentworth early (next: Feb 2027).

chinese.n: Dragon Boat Race for Literacy 龙舟赛
chinese.s: Teams thunder down the river at Ping Tom every June — lion dances, drums, and food tents on the banks.

fishing.s: THE Chicago shore spot — jumbo perch on the horseshoe, spring coho, fall kings; IL license 16+ (perch closed all July).
Dawn perch and browns on the seawall steps from the Loop — coffee, rod, skyline sunrise.
Rocky edges and quiet beach water with the skyline behind you — smallmouth and the odd cruising salmon.
Coho limits in spring and 20-lb kings in summer out of Burnham Harbor — captain covers gear and license details.
Browns and steelhead cruise the harbor mouth spring and late fall — easy shore access along the lagoon.
The comeback story — smallies now hunt the cleaned-up downtown canyons; toss a tube off the Riverwalk or kayak it.
Stocked largemouth, bluegill, and channel cats a bike ride from anywhere on the northwest side.
Bass and big catfish around the wooded Osaka island — Hyde Park's sleeper water.
Pike, largemouth, and glassy canoe water in the forest preserve a half hour north — IL license required.
The south-side multi-species bet — bass, pike, and perch on the Indiana border water.
Muskie in the shadow of the tollway — Cook County's trophy surprise, with boat rentals in season.

biking.s: The destination — 50+ miles of legit singletrack, ravines, and moraine climbs 40 minutes out; the Midwest benchmark.
45-acre bike park inside city limits — pump tracks, jump lines, and beginner loops on a reclaimed marsh.
Sag Valley singletrack next door to Palos — plus the famous 125 toboggan stairs when you want to hurt on foot.
9.5-mile crushed-limestone loop around Argonne — the gravel-bike staple with actual elevation.
18.5 paved miles from beach to beach with a separated bike lane the whole way — the city's standout ride.
2.7 elevated miles through Wicker Park and Logan Square — art, ramps, and prime people-watching.
20+ paved miles along the river all the way to the Botanic Garden — the classic no-car escape.

CAMBr's big northwest-suburb network: 20-plus miles of flowing and technical wooded singletrack in Hoffman Estates, ridden in directions that switch by day. Main lot on W Central Ave; every trail closes when it rains.

About 5 miles of flowy singletrack — berms, gentle climbs and quick descents — wound around the old Meadowdale International Raceway in Carpentersville. Beginner to intermediate; start at the Silo lot on Route 31.

Portage's 10-mile Outback singletrack — tight switchbacks and real hills for the region, with more trail across the river on the east side — in a 276-acre city park an hour around the lake in Indiana.

social.s: Free lesson, live band, hundreds of strangers dancing in Grant Park — salsa, swing, and Chicago Steppin' nights; solo-friendly by design.

social.n: Steppin' on a Sunday (Truth on the Beach)
social.s: Chicago's own smooth partner dance at a weekly lakefront set with DJ Dre Day — come early, regulars will teach you.
Latin Street's River North salsa night — lesson first, then salsa, bachata, and cumbia across three rooms.
West Loop studio party with a rotation-friendly floor — beginners actually get dances here.
Chicago's longest-running weekly swing social at Dance Center Chicago — beginner lesson at 8p, no partner needed.
Free 6:06a workout with hugs and high-fives — location rotates monthly; the friendliest crowd in fitness.
Thursday summer street market on Asia on Argyle — 50+ food vendors, lion dances, and 5,000 neighbors.

social.n: Geeks Who Drink at Houndstooth Saloon
social.s: Monday pub quiz in Wrigleyville — join a short-handed team and you've made five friends by round three.
600-game library with staff Game Guides who teach — the easiest structured hang in the city.

social.n: Chinese/English Language Corner 中英文角
social.s: Meetup 语言角 swapping Mandarin and English over word games and readings — venue varies, RSVP online.
Beach volleyball leagues under the skyline at North Avenue — sign up solo and get drafted onto a team.

We have been playing this game since 2007. Game Format: 4 vs 4, 3-teams, 1-sub each team. Rotate every 10 min. Thursdays from 5:50p with Soccer Club Chicago: Soccer Mecca! 20 years, still going! at Northshore Baptist Church, Chicago · $8 on Meetup.

We have been playing this game since 2007. Game Format: 4 vs 4, 3-teams, 1-sub each team. Rotate every 10 min. Thursdays from 7:20p with Soccer Club Chicago: Soccer Mecca! 20 years, still going! at Northshore Baptist Church, Chicago · $8 on Meetup.

Let's get together every Tuesday evening for a 3-mile run even breaking out into different pacing groups and distances if need be. Tuesdays from 6:30p with 606 Run Club at Park #567, Chicago · no Meetup fee.
We meet at Movement Lincoln Park. Wednesdays from 6:30p with 606 Climbing at Movement Lincoln Park, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

social.n: 4.5 - 5.5 mile hike out of Irene Hernandez Family Picnic Area
social.s: Wednesdays from 9a with Chicago Northwest Side Hiking at Irene C. Hernandez Family Picnic Grove, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

Lincoln Park Run Club is now going to meet in front of Ludlow Charlingtons Coffee Shop at 2425 N Clark and we will end the run there as well. Sundays from 9a with Lincoln Park Run Club at Ludlow Charlingtons Coffee Shop, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Thursday Night Run: Pilot Project Brewing
social.s: Join us Thursday evenings for a 3-mile run through Logan Square and Wicker Park, ending at Pilot Project Brewing. Thursdays from 7p with 606 Run Club at Pilot Project Brewing, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Saturday Outdoor Soccer Mini-Tournament - Fleet Fields
social.s: This Meetup listing is an advertisement for this game. Saturdays from 11a with Grab A Game Chicago Soccer at Fleet Field - Lincoln Yards, Chicago · no Meetup fee.
Free pickup soccer on Sunday mornings at Horner Park! Sundays from 10a with Red Line SG Pickup Soccer and Watch Parties at Horner Park, Chicago · no Meetup fee.
Fridays from 7p with 【 J-KURU CHICAGO 】Evening Japanese Conversation! at Nimble, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Spanish Language meetup in Logan Square
social.s: Come join us for a Spanish Language meetup at the Dill Pickle. We will meet at the Dill Pickle Food Co-op in Logan Square (2746 N Milwaukee Ave) on Thursday, February 16th from 6pm-8pm. Thursdays from 6p with Chicago Spanish Meetup Group at The Dill Pickle Food Co-op, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

We meet at the bar, start the run at 6:35pm, and then meet back at the bar by about 7:10pm. Our typical route is around 5k. Wednesdays from 6:30p with Chicago Beer Runners at Kirkwood, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

We meet at the bar, start the run at 6:35pm, and then meet back at the bar by about 7:10pm to eat, drink, and be merry. Feel free to extend or cut short the run as you see fit. Mondays from 6:30p with Chicago Beer Runners at Wild Goose Bar & Grill, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Meet New People Bar Crawl Chicago - Admission, Welcome Shots & More!
social.s: Saturdays from 9p with Fun People - Fun Events! - Chicago at Wrigleyville, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

social.n: Learn and play board games on Monday nights!
social.s: Come play all kinds of board games on Monday nights! You're not expected to know any of the games as we're always happy to do teach-and-plays. Mondays from 5:30p with Chicago Tabletop & Board Games at Monochrome Brewing, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

remote.s: 8th floor of the old Marshall Field and Company building at 24 E Washington St, a short walk from Millennium Park. The day pass is for one guest, no membership: shared lounges, fast Wi-Fi, coffee & tea, filtered water, kitchen, print/scan/copy and a staffed host desk. Privacy booths for calls; meeting rooms from ≈$63/hr. M–F 9a–5p.

Suite 1700 at 125 S Clark St in the Financial District, above the Sterling Food Hall. The day pass covers common areas M–F 8:30a–5p; members get 24/7 building access. Phone booths, A/V meeting rooms ($60/hr), printing & scanning, free coffee & tea and discounted parking. Floating members can drop into Workbox's other Chicago locations.

Third floor of The Hoxton at 200 N Green St, in Fulton Market. Fast Wi-Fi, a members' café pouring barista coffee (bottomless tea and coffee on a day pass), printers on each floor, phone booths, and for members a terrace and rooftop pool. Day-pass holders don't get meeting rooms, and passes are one person only. The $150 Side Hustler plan covers 4:30p–midnight weekdays and all weekend.
remote.b: Main canteen closes to members for private events several times a week

remote.s: Floors 6–7 of One Chicago at 750 N State St, upstairs from a Life Time athletic club. The lounge day pass buys open tables and quiet phone booths for calls, with Wi-Fi, print/scan/copy, drip coffee and tea, and a kitchen. You can rent a monitor for $25 a day. LifeCafe and a Whole Foods are in the building. Reception M–F 9a–5p; paid garage parking.
remote.p: Lounge day pass ≈$55 · dedicated desk from $549/mo
remote.b: Phone booths see heavy use throughout the space

remote.s: Suite 3300 at 20 N Clark St, a block from Daley Plaza. A cheap Loop drop-in with free coffee & tea, privacy booths, lockers, a kitchen, a printer and A/V-equipped meeting rooms for 6–10. M–F 8:30a–5p; closed weekends.
remote.p: Day pass from $25 · meeting room from $60/hr

remote.s: Chicago's central library, at 400 S State St in the South Loop. Free Wi-Fi, public computers (a daily guest pass if you have no CPL card) and printing from your own device, cash only and b&w only. Study rooms for one or two people hold up to 4 hours a week, booked up to two weeks ahead; bring photo ID. Mon–Thu 9–8, Fri–Sat 9–5, Sun 1–5.
remote.b: Calm; quiet study tables from secluded to open, group rooms bookable

remote.s: Branch at 122 N Aberdeen St, steps from the Fulton Market coworking cluster. Five reservable study rooms on the 2nd floor, two larger meeting rooms, free Wi-Fi and CPL's printing. Hours are staggered: Mon & Wed 10–6, Tue & Thu 12–8, Fri–Sat 9–5, Sun 1–5.

Huge, open bakery-café at 216 N Peoria St in the West Loop, open seven days. The Infatuation says you can count on great Wi-Fi and an outlet. Small tables for solo work and couches for groups, plus pastries good enough to justify a second coffee.
remote.b: Seating gets tight at peak hours; go off-peak for a table

remote.s: Quiet neighborhood café at 946 N Orleans St, in northwest River North. Strong Wi-Fi and a calm room make it a good place to work in the morning. A short walk from Life Time Work if you'd rather pay for a desk later in the day.
remote.b: Quiet and work-friendly early; busier later in the morning

remote.s: The 1897 landmark at 78 E Washington St, across Michigan Ave from Millennium Park. Admission is free, Wi-Fi is free to all, and there are tables, couches and wall outlets in the lobbies. Come for a few hours under the Tiffany dome, not a full day of calls. Open daily 10a–5p.
remote.b: Plenty of seating areas; free tours draw groups Thu and Fri at 1:15p

remote.s: Chef Sujan Sarkar's Indian-inspired café at 328 S Jefferson St, by Union Station on the Loop/West Loop line. The Infatuation lists free Wi-Fi, printing and big windows, but warns it gets loud at mealtimes. Chai, coffee and French-leaning pastries; daytime hours only, closed Sundays.
remote.b: Limited seating; weekday off-peak hours are calmest

events.s: Donizetti's comic opera, conducted by Enrique Mazzola and directed by Mariame Clément. Six performances at the Lyric Opera House make an easy dressed-up date night.
Nikki Glaser plays three nights of her new tour at the Chicago Theatre, including an added Sunday show.
The 30th season of the German-style holiday market in the Loop: Glühwein in the collectible boot mug, bratwurst and handmade ornaments. Free entry; many vendors are cash-only.
Millions of lights strung through the free zoo, 4:30–9p. Tickets run $7–$20 by night; most Mondays are free with registration.
The parade steps off at Oak St at 5:30p and lights up Michigan Ave block by block, then fireworks over the river around 7:30p. Watch the finale from Wacker Dr.
An Original Six matchup the day after Thanksgiving at the United Center. Come early for the anthem; the roar is the best part of a Hawks game.

events.n: Brent Faiyaz: I Spent the Night with Brent Faiyaz
events.s: The R&B star's limited arena run opens in Chicago, ahead of only Brooklyn and LA.
The Joffrey's holiday Nutcracker at the Lyric Opera House, matinees and evenings through Dec 27. It's the city's essential holiday ballet, and tickets run about $50–$171.
The NFL's oldest rivalry on Christmas Day at Soldier Field, a noon kickoff streamed on Netflix. Dress for lakefront wind.

events.n: New Year's Eve Fireworks at Navy Pier
events.s: A free 10-minute midnight show over the lake to ring in 2027. Lakefront Trail spots near the pier fill up fast, so bundle up and arrive early.

events.n: Lunar New Year Parade 春节游行 (Year of the Goat)
events.s: Chinatown's parade for the Year of the Goat 羊年: lion and dragon dances, firecrackers and floats up Wentworth from 24th St at 1p. Dim sum on Wentworth afterward.
Ali Wong brings her new stand-up tour to the Chicago Theatre for two nights.

events.n: Ali Siddiq: The Custom Fit Tour
events.s: The Houston storyteller's arena-size stand-up set at Wintrust Arena in the South Loop. Doors 6p; tickets via Ticketmaster.

events.n: Stevie Wonder: Songs in the Key of Life 50th Anniversary
events.s: Stevie Wonder plays his 1976 soul classic Songs in the Key of Life in full at the United Center, one of only a handful of U.S. stops on the anniversary tour.
The Scottish comic brings Bitter, his 13th solo show, to the landmark Auditorium Theatre. Ages 16+; doors open an hour before showtime.
Week 11 NFL home game at Soldier Field on the lakefront, the Bears' first game back from their bye. Noon kickoff; flex scheduling can still move it.
An illuminated after-dark trail through the Glencoe garden, with timed tickets, 4:30–10:30p most nights (last entry 8:45p). Prices vary by date, many under $30; 21+ nights 12/10 and 1/1.

events.n: Illumination: Tree Lights at The Morton Arboretum
events.s: The Arboretum's 14th season of lit-up trees and light installations along a walking route in Lisle. Timed tickets from $22 for adult nonmembers; model-train add-on $9.

events.n: A Christmas Carol at Goodman Theatre
events.s: The Goodman's 49th annual staging of the Dickens classic in the Albert Theatre, with Tim Hopper playing Scrooge for the first time. A sensory-friendly matinee runs 12/27.
The menu features dishes such as spicy chicken gizzards, pork kidneys, beef aorta, and quail eggs. Saturday from 7p with Adventurous Eating at Liuyishou Hotpot(Chicago) 刘一手火锅 (芝加哥) · $2 on Meetup.

events.n: Lake Front Trail Hike -Start to Finish
events.s: Lake Front Trail Hike -Start to Finish Saturday Nov. The station is 1/4 mile from the start of the trail at 2500 East 71st Street. Saturday from 8:06a with Chicago Appalachian Trail Hiking Club at Lake Front Trail Head (South Shore), Chicago · no Meetup fee.

Check out the new high-tops in the right nook of the bar, for our own private hangout spot All levels and dialects of Chinese are invited for a bi-weekly conversation club. Monday from 6p with INT'L CAFE Chicago at Nine Bar, Chicago · no Meetup fee.
We’re hitting the court this fall for a tournament with a purpose. Saturday from 12p with The - Program at Intentional Sports, Chicago · no Meetup fee.
Join us for a casual afternoon at Frank and Mary's Tavern in Chicago! Saturday from 3p with Singles Who Mingle at Frank and Mary's Tavern, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

events.n: Alice & Friends' Vegan Kitchen Single Mingle Luncheon
events.s: Alice & Friends' Vegan Kitchen has a diverse menu and a lot of flare. Saturday from 12p with Chicago Vegetarians & Vegans 20’s - 40’s at Alice & Friends' Vegan Kitchen, Chicago · no Meetup fee.
Wednesday from 7p with Chicago Seafood and Fish Lovers at Indie Cafe Sushi Thai, Chicago · $3 on Meetup.

awesome food and drinks and live band karaoke. Tuesday from 8p with ! Chicago Is My Oyster! There Is Always More To Explore! at All Star Seafood and sports, Chicago · no Meetup fee.
Join us for an immersion experience right at the Chicago Athletic Club! Sunday from 12p with Fluent in the City Meetup Group at Chicago Athletic Association · no Meetup fee.

events.n: The Heavy! Game night in West Town
events.s: Come spend an afternoon enjoying some of the more complex games the world of board gaming has to offer! Each event, we'll feature a handful of games that will be hitting the tables. Saturday from 5p with Chicago Tabletop & Board Games at Spellbound Games, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

If you haven't joined our table before, this is a good time to start playing or return -- we have space on the team. Tuesday from 7:15p with Chicago South Loop Explorers at Half Sour, Chicago · no Meetup fee.

iceskating.n: Maggie Daley Park Ice Skating Ribbon
iceskating.s: The winding ice ribbon in Maggie Daley Park runs Nov 13, 2026 to Mar 7, 2027 in timed two-hour sessions sold online in blocks (released at noon). Rentals are $17 Mon–Thu and $21 Fri–Sun and holidays; your own skates cost $5, or free at the first session of the day (11a weekdays, 8a weekends).

Millennium Park's Michigan Ave rink returns Nov 20, 2026 and runs to Jan 31, 2027, weather permitting, daily 11a–10:30p. Admission is free, but skating needs a reservation, which the city says it will post in the coming weeks. Weekend 9a lessons include free rentals. Pair it with the Christmas tree and holiday market.

The Park District's year-round indoor rink at McFetridge Sports Center in North Center's California Park. This fall's adult skates (18+) run Mon, Wed and Fri noon–1:30p for $4, with pre-registration required. Also on the calendar: a holiday exhibition Dec 13 and a December Slow Flow session Dec 21.

Hyde Park's outdoor Park District rink on the Midway, south of the University of Chicago quads. It opens with the other neighborhood rinks on Nov 27 and typically runs into mid-February. Admission is free and rentals are $7; open skate needs pre-registration. A community bonfire is set for Dec 8.

West Ridge's outdoor Park District rink at 6601 N Western Ave, opening Nov 27 and typically running to mid-February. Free admission, $7 rentals and required pre-registration, like the city's other neighborhood rinks. A Dec 29 park bonfire is on the calendar, and Devon Ave's restaurants are a few blocks south.

iceskating.n: Morgan Park Sports Center Ice Rink
iceskating.s: The Park District's other year-round indoor sheet, at 115th and Western on the far South Side. Adult open skate (18+) runs Mon, Tue, Thu and Fri noon–2p for $5 this fall; pre-registration is required, and all-ages sessions are posted with the rink's programs.

The Blackhawks' practice home on the Near West Side by the United Center, formerly Fifth Third Arena. Public skate sits on the posted calendar most days, often early afternoon (12:30p or 2:50p in early November), between team practices, freestyle ice, stick & puck and late-night adult leagues.

Skokie's park-district arena, where Scott Hamilton and Stan Mikita once skated, open for public skating year-round with no reservations: pay $7 plus $4 rental at the desk. Holiday extras include Thanksgiving-weekend sessions Nov 27–28, a Grinch skate Dec 6 and Skate with Santa Dec 12.

iceskating.n: Robert Crown Community Center ice rink
iceskating.s: Evanston's city rink on Main St. Public skating is $10 (18+) or $6 (17 and under), rentals $4, and tickets go on sale online seven days ahead; DJ skate nights cost $11/$7 and are sold at the door only. A $110 annual pass covers regular sessions. The rink stays around 60°F, so dress warm.

skating.s: Since 2018 the lakefront has run as an 18-mile Bike Trail beside an 18.5-mile Pedestrian Trail, asphalt and concrete from South Shore to Edgewater past Navy Pier and the beaches. The Park District is patching and seal-coating it one section at a time over the coming months, working north from 63rd St to Foster, so expect signed work zones.

The elevated 2.7-mile Bloomingdale Trail runs from the Ridgeway trailhead to Walsh Park above Bucktown and Wicker Park with no street crossings, and TrailLink lists it for inline skating. Riders call it smooth but extremely busy on nice days, so skate it early. Open daily 6a–11p.

skating.n: Maggie Daley Park skating ribbon (wheels season)
skating.s: Out of ice season the winding ribbon becomes a downtown roller loop: bring your own wheels 6a–9p, or rent rollerblades or Micro scooters at $10 plus tax per half hour. Skaters have right of way over walkers. The 2026 wheels season ended Oct 1 for ice-making and returns after the ice closes in March.

A 25.5-mile asphalt greenway along the North Branch of the Chicago River from Foster Ave to the Botanic Garden, with free forest-preserve lots along the way. An August 2026 review flags blind curves, fast road cyclists and wide crossings at Golf, Dempster, Touhy and Devon; the east side of the Skokie Lagoons loop is the quieter half.

A 16.2-mile asphalt trail along the Calumet-Sag Channel from the I&M Canal Trail at Lemont east to Alsip, flat through the prairie stretch past Sag Quarries and hillier in the woods east of Teason's Woods. Reviewers call it beautiful and quiet but note grit at road crossings and some worn pavement; about half is shaded.

A 7.6-mile South Side rail-trail from Dan Ryan Woods to Whistler Woods, named for the champion Black cyclist. The north end rides the old rail embankment with an overpass at 83rd St, and riders call the surface flat and well kept. Between 95th and 105th it runs on city streets, and several wide crossings need care.

A 21.6-mile asphalt rail-trail from Joliet to Chicago Heights that runs right through downtown Frankfort's shops and cafés. Reviewers describe very straight, smooth pavement east of Harlem Ave through wetlands and woods; the westernmost 8 miles climb a gentle 200 ft, so the Frankfort–Park Forest end is the easier roll.

A flat 9.8-mile asphalt path from Highland Park to Lake Bluff, squeezed between US 41 and the rail line under power lines. No views, but long straightaways, mile markers and few crossings make it a North Shore speed and interval route. Reviewers reported repair closures around miles 6–8 in 2022–23, so check before driving up.
